## Introduction

For this portfolio you'll be creating a visualisation of the distribution of the number of people using the bridge on He Ara Kotahi walkway per day in Palmerston North.

We use data from one year which we've summarised by all users per day:

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
walk_cycle <- read_csv("https://www.massey.ac.nz/~jcmarsha/data/pncc_cycle_counts/he_ara_kotahi_one_year.csv") |>
  group_by(Date) |>
  summarise(Count = sum(Count)) |>
  mutate(Day = wday(Date, label=TRUE))
```

## Requirements

Download the `portfolio02.qmd` template file below and write code using the `walk_cycle` data to produce ONE chart of the **distribution** of the number of people using the bridge per day.

**It is your choice as to which chart type you choose to use. There is not necessarily a "best" chart type.**

 - Ensure you fill in your name in the author field.
 - Your chart should clearly show the **distribution** of the number of people using the bridge for each of the 7 days separately.
 - Consider carefully what the "story" of your chart is and use the title/subtitle or annotation to help highlight the story.
 - Ensure your chart has clear labels.
 - You should submit the `portfolio.qmd` file to the stream dropbox.
 - Make sure that it renders correctly before submission.
 
## Grading rubric

You will be graded out of 10 based on:

 - Your submission must be reproducible and render without errors or warnings (2 marks).
 - Your submission must include your name in the author field and the code for your chart (2 marks).
 - Your chart should satisfy the requirements given above (6 marks).
